note: The external-dependency carrier, machine-readable (SPEC.md beside this
file is the prose half; kogaki#55).
checks/check-external-deps.sh READS these lists rather than restating
them — this file is the single carrier, so amending the contract is one
edit and never a two-copy divergence. Same arrangement as
The enumeration itself lives in deps/registry.json. This file says what
an entry must LOOK like; it never says which capabilities exist.

needed_by.rationale: a capability nothing needs is not a dependency; a non-empty consumer list is what makes a stale entry removable rather than permanent

when_decidable.answers_is: the question the command's output settles, in one line

when_not_decidable.rationale: SPEC.md §3 — a typed 'none: <why>' is a first-class value and evidence; an omitted field is not. A partial audit reporting only its positives is indistinguishable from a complete one.

fallback.rationale: SPEC.md §4 — dependency N+1 is uncovered by any enumeration; what is avoidable is its being uncovered SILENTLY. product-lab@ed47fbd3 LESSONS.md:103.

fails_on: an entry missing a required field
a verification block whose decidable flag disagrees with the fields present
an empty verification.reason on a non-decidable entry
a registry file that does not parse
never_fails_on: an unmet dependency — a decidable verification that reports absent
check_semantics.rationale: SPEC.md §5 — conformance is the check's subject; whether the world currently satisfies a dependency is a report. Same split as checks/registry.json's consult-receipts entry: 'Fails only on a malformed receipt, never on the count.'
renders_explicitly: each decidable verification's result, present or absent
each non-decidable entry's reason, rather than omitting the row
an empty registry's zero — the carrier may port ahead of its first entry, and a silent pass would be indistinguishable from a check that did not run
